text:
maria: Quickstart run — following the pagination example in the JS quickstart and I start seeing 429s after a few pages, then the client keeps retrying forever. Anyone seen this?

kevin: Which SDK version? we fixed a retry loop in 0.9.x but pagination had a separate prefetch behavior.

maria: Using 0.9.2 (npm). Snippet is basically:

sam: ```js
for await (const page of client.paginate('listMessages', { pageSize: 50 })) {
  await process(page.items)
}
```

maria: Logs show repeated 429 then a few successful pages then 429 again. Also seeing `Retry-After: 3` in the response headers. The retries keep happening and overall throughput tanks.

sam: Sounds like the paginator is prefetching next pages concurrently and the global rate limiter is counting all inflight requests, hitting the quota. The client retry/backoff currently doesn't cancel prefetches when a 429 with Retry-After arrives.

kevin: Confirmed. JS SDK paginator defaults to prefetch=2 and internal concurrency for perf. We didn't wire per-request `Retry-After` handling into the prefetch loop, so it will keep issuing the prefetched requests and then retry them independently.

alex: Short-term workaround: set paginate options to serialize requests: `client.paginate('listMessages', { pageSize: 50, concurrency: 1, prefetch: 0 })` or set `maxRetries: 2` in the client config. That should avoid the prefetch-induced 429 storm.

jen: Is this a quota (tokens/second) or per-route QPS? Both matter — prefetching multiple pages multiplies token usage, which trips the global token quota even if each route has its own per-route soft-limit. We should document the interaction in quickstart.

maria: Workaround helped (concurrency:1). Can we also respect `Retry-After` header in the paginator so it stops prefetching for that user session?

kevin: Yes — plan: 1) Have paginator check for `Retry-After` and pause prefetch for that duration. 2) Make `respectRateLimits` opt-in in JS (python already has a similar flag). 3) Add logging so quickstarts show when prefetching is disabled due to rate limits.

sam: I pushed a tiny repro app to a gist showing the pattern (prefetch=2 -> 429s under token-limited test). Link: https://gist.github.com/sam/repro-prefetch-429 (demo script uses local throttle to simulate token quota).

deploy-bot: Notification: small doc update PR (devex/quickstart) deployed to staging at 2026-02-03T16:12:07Z.

jen: Filed SDK issue #4122 with reproduction steps and an initial patch proposal. I'll add a quickstart note and a sample config demonstrating safe defaults for new users.

kevin: Temporary patch suggestion for anyone hitting this in prod: set `maxRetries: 2`, add explicit `retryDelay` exponential backoff, and disable prefetch. Example config:

```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY,
  maxRetries: 2,
  retryDelay: (attempt) => Math.min(10000, 300 * 2 ** attempt)
})

for await (const page of client.paginate('listMessages', { concurrency: 1, prefetch: 0 })) {
  // safe single-threaded pagination
}
```

maria: Thanks all — can we add a short note in the JS quickstart and the sample app repo that explains the prefetch/rate-limit interaction? This tripped up a few new users in my onboarding session.

jen: Yep, I'll update the quickstart text and the sample app. Also adding a little checkbox in the quickstart "if you see 429s during pagination" with the workaround.

alex: Long-term: think about a client-level knob `respectRateLimits: 'auto' | true | false` where `auto` uses server headers and a shared token bucket across paginator instances.

maria: Awesome. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
